notes.title: Version 1.0.2.4 - Improved performance and character control
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/e581cd240ed7ae866cc41cf6098fa817e12f39f0.png[/img]

Hallo Ellarians,

We just uploaded a new version with major overall performance improvement, reduced loading time between map travel, and a better character movement and jumping.

One of our biggest changes was to reduce the impact of having a large number of characters in the same place. We introduced a new system that changes the character resolution dynamically based on their clothing and complexity, and their distance from the camera. This system reduces the character performance issues by 80% and [b]increases the frame rate by as much as 15 extra frames per second.[/b]

In addition, we went over thousands of textures and items optimized them. This optimizations [b]increases the game performance by 25%-50%, the required memory by 25%, and the loading time between maps by as much as 30%. [/b]

As a result of these changes, you should notice a significant improvement to LoE performance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/70782c0348bbc563b8f890f7416f5622e8d9079d.jpg[/img]

Another improvement that we've made is to the character movement and jumping, as well as the camera following the player. These changes makes sure that you will have a more intuitive and smoother movement and jumping, without changing too much of the character stats.

Our next goal is to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/621070/announcements/detail/3612480255012641486]improve the story line and quests[/url], In the meanwhile, We wish to thank you for your feedback. We will continue to optimize and improve other parts of LoE as much as we can.

[b]Version 1.0.2.4 Changes[/b] [i](7/2/23)[/i]
[list]
[*] Reduced NPC performance cost by 50% near the camera
[*] Reduced NPC performance cost by up to 90% when far away from camera
[*] Multiple texture and model reduction, by up to 75% of the original size without losing graphics
[*] Increased overall graphic performance by up to 50% (depending on the region)
[*] Reduced the size of the game and memory (RAM) by 25%
[*] Reduced game loading time between regions by up to 30% (depending on the region)
[*] Improved character movement and jumping
[*] Improved camera following the player in third person
[/list]

notes.title: Planned quest and story updates.
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/e3cd721d3012ca0e712ea9ce29275725ebe490f1.png[/img]

Hallo Elarians, 
We wanted to share with you some information about the upcoming quest updates. These updates will balance Legends of Ellaria and add more fun with less grinding. We're also going to change some quests and lore based on your feedbacks. 

First, [b]we're considering to remove some of [i]Prisca's quests[/i][/b]. This will allow you to progress on the Mage's path much faster. We're also going to add some extra rewards to [i]Prisca's quests[/i].

[b]We're also going to set some of the bandit quests as optional[/b], just in case you'd want to have a quick run to the next chapters. [b]We're also considering to make [i]Free Market[/i]quest as optional[/b] , since you can expand your kingdom without using a market.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/205a3d4172751e047721019e985111ee09db00ca.png[/img]

[b]We're also considering to shorten several main and sub quests[/b]. One of them is the [i]Ancient Orb[/i] quest, which sends you to 11 different places. We loved the story behind the quest, but some of you complained that its too long to finish. We're considering shortening several of these quests without losing their reward, such as [i]Magical Enquiries[/i] and [i]Thinning the herd[/i].

We're also going to make quests more fluent and focused on one goal, so that you'll focus on the story and on progressing your kingdom.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/4eab26b59fe1ec3117732432c8e7819cf775d8cf.jpg[/img]

There are lots of other changes, and we're still testing these changes. We've also made progress on the character mechanics, and on the general maintenance. Our next version should include the character mechanics.

Please tell us your opinion and suggestion about quests, quest reward ideas and other things you'd like to change, or if you'd like to add new quests to the game.

In the meanwhile, thank you for your feedback and for your support.

One of our main goals is to allow Legends of Ellaria to lower its system requirement. For that, we're in the process of improving and remastering all of our models and textures. notes.title: New mods, new modding, and a one week 85% discount!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/d1c50aa44c58f9e64c1c078331ad2cd345a1dba4.jpg[/img]

Hallo Ellarians,

We've just achieved a new milestone by finishing the new modding system and adding multiple new mods. And as a bonus, we've started a one-week 85% discount!  

Based on your feedback and some of our ideas, we've added a few useful and fun mods to Legends of Ellaria. Although these mods are not official and may not be balanced, we sure had a lot of fun playing with them. Here are some of them:

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2842155285&searchtext=][u]Possess[/u][/url]
You can now possess any person in the world, immediately gaining control, inventory and basic skills. You can also possess heroes to gain full combat and skill abilities.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2842158306&searchtext=][u]Hardcore Mode[/u][/url]
Is the base combat too boring? Try out a more challenging difficulty.

This mod increases all weapons and spells base damage to 200%, both for you and for your enemies. This means that combat is shorter and deadlier and armor is less effective. Because of that you'll have to be more tactical as some creatures may now kill you with a single hit.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2842156146&searchtext=][u]Fast Runner[/u][/url]
Tired of running from location to location? This mod removes all stamina cost of sprinting and increases your sprint speed, allowing you to explore the map faster.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2842158694&searchtext=][u]The Swarm[/u][/url]
Your enemies are determined to destroy your kingdom. They will fight you to the last breath.

This mod increases Bandits, Northerners, Dark ones and Zombies invasion time by 500%. This means that your kingdom will be invaded on average every three days or so. In some cases, you'll be attacked by multiple armies at the same time. You will have to defend your towns and outposts while quickly expanding your kingdom and economy if you want to survive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/46d415fba21c660ee748e9dda93b3b7429a9619f.png[/img]

We've made some other minor mods, and we've also released a new version with some minor bug fixes. Please let us know if you'd like us to add more mods. In the meanwhile, we thank you for your support and feedback.

notes.notes:

We want to thank everyone who gave us feedback. Even after its release, you've helped us polish, balance, and add essential parts to Legends of Ellaria.

[*] Balanced and tweaked the Druid class to be an unstoppable support class.

[*] Balanced and tweaked the elemental mage class to deliver more raw damage per spell. 

[*] Balanced and tweaked the ranger class to have more accuracy at earlier levels, draw arrows faster, deliver more damage and consume less stamina per shot. The ranger class is most dangerous in higher levels, especially when supported by your soldiers.

[*] Balanced and tweaked kingdom management to allow you to build larger kingdoms and use strategic locations. Multiple buildings stats and kingdom management cap penalty were changed based on community requests and rebalancing.

[*] Tweaked the Kingdom research tree to give more versatility to economics and management tree.

[*] Balanced and tweaked weaker military units, such as militia, to allow for an easier start and an easier kingdom defense through your progress.

[*] Added a "Demolish" button to city construction

[*] Chapter I is unlocked even if you didn't finish the tutorial.

[*] Changed and tweaked multiple quests and dialogues.

[*] Improved the AI and path finding.

notes.title: Version 1.0.1.11 - Combat Classes Balancing
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/e9826197ed08d93a713f826e4de6faed56ce1258.png[/img]

Hallo Ellarians,

We just uploaded a new version with major balancing to combat damages and stats and a few minor fixes to dialogues and combat mechanics.

We took some of your suggestions and made some extensive tests to make sure that all the player classes are balanced. Some of the classes were weaker than others, and some, like the mage class, were strong at the beginning but would not scale properly as you level up.

Our biggest change was to the ranger class, as we've significantly increased the damage and accuracy at lower levels. We've made sure that the ranger class will be much deadlier and that you won't have to be level 15 or above to gain high bow accuracy

In addition, we fixed a persistent fire enchantment effect that would stay after the effect was done. We also made sure that the player will be able to remove the fire enchantment effect by casting the "Minor Dispel." We also fixed several issues with the merchant guild dialogues.

We wish to thank you for your feedback. We will continue to fix and tweak any issue we'll find and balance and add things by your suggestion. Also, stay tuned for the Necromancer DLC.

notes.title: Legends of Ellaria roadmap and plans
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/d1c50aa44c58f9e64c1c078331ad2cd345a1dba4.jpg[/img]
Hallo Ellarians,

First of all, we want to thank every one of you for your support over the years, and for your endless feedbacks and playtests, your forum and discord votes, chats, and suggestions.

We released Legends of Ellaria several months ago and received different varieties of feedback. We figured that some people might not connect with the way we designed and balanced the multi-genre gameplay style, but we received more feedback about that than expected.

So what now?
After years of constant development, sometimes 24/7 work(a dream job, what are you gonna do 😊 ), we focused on bugs and fixes while managing the team size and overall projects that Larkon Studio does. notes.title: Some Q&A
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/a937fb303e8d1c208857a130b354ee61eaa712ab.jpg[/img]

Greetings, Ellarians!

We've compiled a list of questions about our history and about our future plans. Have fun!

[b]Q: Now that Legends of Ellaria is in full release, will the development continue.[/b]
A: Yes, it will. We are constantly working on improving and optimizing the game mechanics to run faster and with as few bugs as possible. In addition, we're working on some extra features and DLC's. One of which is the long awaited Necromancer DLC.

[b]Q: Will you improve or change the game's main mechanics, such as the combat system or real-time strategy?[/b]
A: We're not planning to make any drastic changes beyond optimisations and tweaks to any main mechanics. We're flattered that our combat system and other mechanics were compared to AAA games, but we're a small team and our concept to link first person mechanics to real-time strategy and kingdom management mechanics together in a single game has its limitations. We are personally happy with the results and with the gameplay, as it exceeded our expectations.

[b]Q: What inspired Legends of Ellaria's main story?[/b]
A: The concept was written a long time ago, during Legends of Ellaria's basic design. We drew a storyboard that spanned between several chapters. The initial story was comic, along with some story driven twists, such as a quest to defeat a monster to ally yourself with your neighbors, only to find out that the beast is a peaceful, huge creature that just misunderstood your neighbor's intention. We later changed the main story to be more serious, as it would miss out on the fantasy and lore aspects if it was too comic.

Because of our main story's complexity and multiple locations, we were worried that we wouldn't be able to design all the locations that you go through. However, we managed to add Marra, Greenside, the northerners' lands, the ancient beast, Arag's castle,  the dark one's realms, and the Aunaloth monster through the four chapters in the final release. We were happy with the results and with the different atmospheres and location designs.

[b]Q: There were talks about other features, such as siege weapons, races, etc. Where do we stand on that?[/b]
A: Our goal was to build the core of Legends of Ellaria and advance with our community's feedback. We learned which features were more important than the other through our community posts and votes and made a list of planned features by priority. Unfortunately, we couldn't add all these planned features. 

Some of these features are the siege weapons feature and horses, which were added to a beta version in the legacy but were later removed because of technical limitations or game-breaking mechanics. Others were unique races, such as dwarves, which were too time-consuming to add. On the other hand, we managed to add features which we didn't think we'll be able to add, such as the three mage classes, multiple dimensions, and more.

We are now planning to add some of these features through DLC's, and we're currently working on the Necromancer DLC. We will try to add as many of the requested / planned features as we can. 

[b]Q: Community speaking, how did the community contribute, besides the general feedbacks?[/b]
A: Our community was the backbone of our progress from the early stage of development. We started with general community channels before we released the early access, which grew and participated over time to help us stay on the right track. Our community also participated in votes for features and priorities, as well as actual design concept votes. 

Besides that, many of our members helped us with more than feedbacks. Some of them are Bardon, who helped translate much of our lore and dialogues and wrote some of Legends of Ellaria's stories. Others are Nito-Murray, who helped as a community moderator and also tested early versions before others. We also had many other volunteers who helped us test versions of the game before their official release through the beta testing program.

We want to thank our community. Your support helped us shape Legends of Ellaria.

[b]Q: What is Larkon Studio's plans for the future ? Will there be a Legends of Ellaria 2 ? Or any other game?[/b]
A: We're looking into designing other games, including a design for Legends of Ellaria 2, set in the past during the ancients and dark ones wars. We don't have any information at this time, though. 

Meanwhile, we're working on some DLC's for Legends of Ellaria, including the Necromancer DLC. We'll post more information on that in the following weeks.



That is it for today. Let us know If you have any other questions. Also, we will post another patch in the following days with some useful fixes. And again, thank you for your interest. See you in Ellaria,

Larkon Studio

notes.title: New dungeons and exploration and the upcoming Beta
notes.notes:
Greetings Ellarians! As you surely have noticed, we’ve kept our heads low for several weeks because we were hard at work on some new content that will be released soon. This week, we just completed and polished a new feature we mentioned a few times before. Legends of Ellaria is getting dungeons! 

As you may remember from previous dev and lore blogs, the Ancients left behind a multitude of structures and buildings. Among them, there are many underground constructions – mighty dungeons which purpose is now lost time, but which, thanks to the powerful technology and magic that the Ancients possessed, are still more or less intact and operative. 

They are quite dangerous, though. The Ancients left behind powerful traps and magical machines protecting their bearings. Some are comparatively simple – they will shoot you a simple firebolt if you get too near. Others will fire strong spells that can kill an unprepared hero in a single hit. And they can’t be disabled or disarmed – you will have to find a way to destroy them altogether. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/a5361a05b2b88309a6fe7fbdffa935622387900e.gif[/img]

But traps aren’t the only hazard you will find in Ancient-made dungeons. They have been desert for so long that many different creatures have colonized them, and you will have to fight them to advance. However, fortune favors the brave – they who dare to explore one of these ruins and manage to clear them up can find treasures, gold, Riftstone, even Ancient devices that can be sold or given to your Librarian to increase their research. 

Under the land of Ellaria, there are also vast complexes of natural caves. Riftstone can be found there too, as well as rich ores and sometimes treasures – all this can change the course of your kingdom for good. But, just as it happens with Ancient ruins, these caves tend to be inhabited and protected. Bandits and goblins make them their lairs, and you will have to face scores of them to get to their deepest levels. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/afac22e110c898886624e55795c7ca9e6dba4fcb.gif[/img]

In a nutshell: these places are dangerous and challenging, but they offer great rewards too. Their treasures can be the icing of the cake for wise kings who are great managers of their kingdoms – but also a way to balance things for more action-oriented kings, who favor personal strength and valor over strategy and resource management.. Exploring these areas and clearing them, as well as completing quests given by your advisor, will earn you enough wealth to build anything and hire an army to solve most problems that your kingdom may face. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/0a61e7fec49d445fa80ef115e5dcdfc35dd31b4f.gif[/img]

There will be many different dungeons in Ellaria – some bigger than others, some more dangerous but with better rewards. We hope you have a great time exploring and clearing them! 

Our plan is to update the game with this new content within a couple of weeks at most; we will let you know here as the date approaches. Thanks for reading, and may your adventures in Ellaria lead you to glory!

notes.title: Upcoming Major Update
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/d1c50aa44c58f9e64c1c078331ad2cd345a1dba4.jpg[/img]

[i][b]The wind howls, and there are strange whispers in the dark. The sound of soft footsteps come from empty, long forsaken rooms. Around a crackling fire, the elders tell stories of old – stories of hags and warlocks, wicked tricksters and evil spirits. Halloween is here, and the spooky season comes to Ellaria too! [/b][/i]

It’s been some time since our last update; we’ve been hard at work developing new content for the game, and we’re really excited to share with you some details about the next update of Legends of Ellaria. This will be one of the biggest updates in a long long time, so buckle up to check what’s coming to your kingdom! 

[b]New locations to explore [/b]

Ellaria will be even bigger with new maps and locations to explore, with miles of terrain full of new dangers – and rewards for those brave enough to face these challenges. A multitude of new dungeons, caves, camps and villages will be added to the world map. Each new map is 2 in-game miles wide – about 8 times bigger than they were before, and with more things to do than ever! 

[b]New quests and events[/b]

We hope you have not stashed your weapon of choice too far if you felt at some point you were running out of adventures, we’re adding more than one hundred quests and events for you to experience, as well as new items to search! These quests may not only help you to level up your character, but also to affect your kingdom as a whole. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/5949924da5cad6c0c500d7a57fda169a7faa3d1f.jpg[/img]

[b]A new kingdom…[/b]

In the last months we’ve discussed how kingdom management was shaping up – you can read our dev diaries about it here and here. Finally, these features are coming to the game! Mine for resources, construct buildings in your cities (more than 20 new buildings added!) and research technologies to upgrade them, keep your army morale up and win battles to expand your borders.  

[b]…and new ways to rule it [/b]

You can be a ruler with an iron fist, expanding your kingdom through war and conquest, or an adventurer king who goes on special quests. You can hire mercenaries or improve your economy to keep a strong standing army. Real-time strategy battles have been revamped for a better strategic experience. There are many different approaches to governing – follow your heart and instincts to become the most powerful ruler of Ellaria! 

[b]Take detours[/b]

Ruling and going on adventures are just two of the many things you can do in Ellaria. Help your settlers working in the farmlands or mining for resources, talk to them to hear their personal stories, collect Artifacts for the librarian… even the new loading screen has minigames!

[b]That’s is the tip of the iceberg[/b]: just about every feature of the game has received some kind of improvement, a huge step closer in our road towards full release. If all this sounds interesting… we have to say that it is only the beginning, for there is something even bigger coming to Legends of Ellaria: finally, the campaign main story is coming to the game! A story of heroes and villains, politics and intrigues, with many different characters, quests and epic battles, the main story spans through five chapters with multiple choices and side optional missions. In this next major update we’re releasing the first chapter of the main story – but that’s all we can tell you for now. We’ll give you more details about this in a few days, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Ellaria - RTS advanced guide
notes.notes:
Good day, Ellarians!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/7fcaf9663026f4285676683d46105bd1cbac92c8.jpg[/img]

In this week’s dev diary we wanted to go back to a topic we already visited a few weeks back: RTS combat. You might remember that we showed you a sneak peak of it, but considering we have worked on it over the past weeks, adding new features, we’d like to show you how it has evolved until now.
When you approach a battle in the world view, a button will pop-up offering you to join into combat. If you accept, you will enter the battlefield where you can choose between fighting in first-person camera or doing so in the real-time strategy mode. As you know, first-person combat will allow you to issue commands to your army to attack, defend, or follow you. 

But let’s dig deeper into the RTS combat so you can gain an advantage in the battlefield. The first thing to note is that not all of your troops will enter the battlefield. Depending on the strength of your army and the enemy’s you will only get some of your troops and you might be able to use the rest of them as reinforcements later on (note that if your army is too small you will get all of your troops at once, but no reinforcements). So, if you attack a stronger army than yours, you will always find yourself in a weaker position than the enemy. In this case, it might be more responsible to go defensive to try to lose as few troops as possible while inflicting damage to your opponent. Note that the battle will end when one of the sides has lost more than 80% of their army.

To help you fight in RTS mode we have also implemented new features. Positioning is a key aspect in the battlefield so we will give you tools to select and move your troops in an efficient way. One of them is the ability to group your soldiers and bind keys so you can select them in a faster manner. For example, select a group of archers and click Ctrl + number and then click that number and you will be in control of that group. This might be useful to have different groups for your archers or your melee fighters.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/e372ad637d34890a4fc578cbe72be09d942a96eb.jpg[/img]

Speaking of archers, positioning them will be important as they don’t fire on friendly troops. One way to deal great damage with them is by positioning them on a side of the battlefield, so they will have a clear line of view. If you set some melee fighters in a defensive formation in front of them you can set a trap for your enemy, that will fight a shield wall while receiving arrows from their sides.
Commands will also be important in RTS fights. We talked a little bit about this before, bet let us elaborate a bit more about how to do it in a battle. There will be three commands available to players: move, stop, and attack. The move command will move to a location, usually without attacking anything on the way. The stop command will tell the soldiers to stop moving and fight anything near them (though pressing the stop command twice will enter a "defend" mode, in which your soldiers will stop and stand their ground). And finally, the attack command will tell your soldiers to go to a location and fight anything on the way.

You will be able to issue multiple commands so you won’t have to be paying attention to every movement of your army. For example, if you need to outflank your enemy you can issue the following orders: go left, then go north, then attack move. Outflanking is an important maneuver in Legends of Ellaria. When a soldier is hit from behind, he receives double damage, so you should make sure that your soldiers are not attacked from multiple sides. There are easy ways to avoid this, such as selecting a dozen soldiers and tell them to go to a location. They will arrange themselves as a formation pointing to that location.

And that’s it for today. The size of your army, its position on the battlefield, and the commands you issue will be important features of RTS combats. We hope you have learned a little more about it in this week’s dev diary. 


See you next week, Ellarians!

notes.title: Ellaria - RPG/Strategy
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/60b70607ba3e58cddc9ff4881baeb059aabf4dc3.jpg[/img]

Good day, Ellarians!

As you may remember, a few weeks ago we posted a dev diary that explored the combat system. You may recall that Legends of Ellaria is a unique blend of RPG and real-time strategy so each player can approach the game as they prefer. You can get your hands dirty fighting bosses or you may take a calmer perspective looking at combat from an aerial view like you may do in many RTS titles.
This philosophy also applies when considering how to embrace Ellaria’s world. You may choose between playing from a more role-playing perspective or you can focus on strategy, making big decisions, and letting everybody else do the job. It’s your call, but since these genres are very different from each other, we can't design a game where you can play with only one of the genres, and we can't force you to master both.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/15eef62e0fc3d5fbea6c58dcd110673910a0ed81.jpg[/img]

We think we have found an answer to that problem. And that answer is freedom, so players can have multiple ways of doing a task. For instance, there are four different ways to fight a battle. The most obvious is entering into the battlefield to fight in the first-person mode, using your weapon of choice or magic. But let’s pretend you have a sizable army with you: you can point at your enemy, issue commands, and then, simply stay back and enjoy the fight. If you are more into a strategic approach, you can switch to the Real-Time Strategy mode and issue multiple commands to your soldiers. This mode will give you an edge, as you'll be able to defend soldiers, chose the soldiers that will engage in the first wave, and adapt to the battlefield. And lastly, you can resolve the battle by letting your army fight for themselves. Not entering the battlefield is the way of the king, observing from afar and treating every battle as a single move in a larger strategic plan.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/c96c100bcfd7db01b1e9ab281d825dccab37446c.png[/img]

Choices will be present at any point in the game. Think for a minute about exploration. Your character might be entering a new location as part of the main story. Next, he or she will meet one of the villains. Do you want to fight with your well-built character? Or do you prefer to press F2 and let your elite troops handle that enemy? It is your choice.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/e771ea2608820ef30c136b84f7deeb35836ac70e.jpg[/img]

One last thing we want to clarify: this approach not only sticks to battles. It actually can be used when performing any task. You can build a farm and manage it as a strategic location or you can go to that farm, perform quests, meet your fellow farmers, and gather extra food for your kingdom using farm equipment. In the end, you will be the one choosing how to live your life, either as a king or as a self-made hero.

notes.title: Ellaria - World Generation
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/5a5c3ee8583360aa44620457fa691693a3df0480.jpg[/img]

Good day, Ellarians!

Over the last two weeks, we took a tour of the world of Ellaria. First, we visited some of its most gorgeous landscapes and took a look at how the cities of its world will look like. But we also took our time showing indoor spaces such as houses, palaces or dungeons. This week we want to take a different look at Ellaria’s world and how the dev team has worked to make it procedurally generated so it always looks unique to our players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/1a18d2ace0487b53ea26d969ec405e19d4b8ea9e.jpg[/img]

Let’s start talking about the world map. Ellaria is huge and we wanted every region to have a unique flavor. How we managed to accomplish that? We have a set of map templates and a smart slot system that can fill that region with villagers, goblins, bandit camps, or other elements according to the faction that rules that area. This way, every location you visit will look different from the ones at other locations. This also means that you will find unique generated resources or enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/a39c8955915cdf90a0d03eff6e62f4ec00a2bf90.jpg[/img]

To make the world of Ellaria a unique place we had to design a system so each house was different from each other. We have worked on a system that changes its appearance on both the inside and the outside. Each house is connected to the biome it’s built, so when the map generates it, it also adds grass or flowers around it. Houses can have small, medium, or large sizes, and their insides are also procedurally generated. Each one has its own set of furniture and every piece of furniture also generates its items. For example, a bookshelf will have candlelights or books you can read. A cupboard will have cutlery and accessories that you can grab and trade in the market or the blacksmith to get some iron.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/0032e9ae06600befc14d11fbf6a8995cc358fd8f.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29507675/bba4e9cb27261be455b743e45f5ec0969738579e.jpg[/img]

We have also worked to have unique dungeons in Ellaria’s world. They work similarly to our houses. We have a set of around 15 templates but each one of them generates different enemies, chests, and random resources so you won’t find two that look like the same. Speaking of resources, Ellaria is a good place to look and gather them. Resources can be useful if you want to trade them in the market and can also be used for other purposes, such as crafting weapons or armors. Lumber, gold, iron, stone, or food can be collected around Ellaria and you will have to find them at locations where they are supposed to be. So, look for stony structures to get stone or look for gold in bandit camps. You can also mine, chop, and farm to help boost your kingdom’s resources.

There’s one last item that we wanted to talk about today: rift stones. These magical stones are very rare, have great power, and give you very precious resources. You can trade them for gold, for research or to boost your kingdom’s production. But you can also use them to buy golems, activate portals, or craft special weapons. How you use their special power will be up to you… just remember to use it wisely! 
That’s all for today. Ellaria’s world will be full of interesting places to discover and interact with, hidden caves, and interesting people to meet. 

We hope you will be having as much fun exploring every corner of it as we are having while designing it!
